links.comparator_used: Expert clinician fact-checking (3 clinical experts) of the same responses and statements
links.outcome: Accuracy (agreement with experts) and time to complete fact-checking
links.effect: Acne scenario: GPT-4o and OpenBioLLM-70B both 86% agreement with experts. 20 claims: GPT-4o 100%, OpenBioLLM-70B 95%. Time: experts mean 18 (SD 3.74) min, GPT-4o 42 s, OpenBioLLM-70B 33 min.
links.tradeoff: LLM fact-checks missed some safety messages (urgency of stopping isotretinoin, folic acid). OpenBioLLM-70B was slower than the experts and omitted 1 key safety item. The authors conclude that human experts still need to perform additional checks for accuracy and safety.
links.quote: The expert fact-checks took a mean time of 18 (SD 3.74) minutes, GPT-4o took 42 seconds, and OpenBioLLM-70B took 33 minutes.

links.comparator_used: General-purpose GPT-4o compared with the domain-specific biomedical model OpenBioLLM-70B
links.outcome: Fact-checking agreement with human experts, speed, and omissions of safety information
links.effect: 20 claims: GPT-4o 100% vs OpenBioLLM-70B 95% agreement with experts. Acne scenario: both 86%. Time: GPT-4o 42 s vs OpenBioLLM-70B 33 min.
links.tradeoff: The domain-specific model was much slower, diverged from experts on 1 pediatric antihistamine question, and omitted 1 key patient-safety information item.
links.quote: For the set of 20 medical claims, GPT-4o fact-checking had 100% agreement with that of human experts, whereas OpenBioLLM-70B had 95% agreement.

design_hint: LLM automated fact-checking of responses versus human expert review
